title: Week in Orbit
summary: As NASA eyes new headquarters and contemplates a Hubble reboost, the space industry is buzzing with funding rounds and strategic partnerships. Meanwhile, defense tech is stirring, with IPOs on the horizon and a notable uptick in space resilience funding.

themes.title: NASA's Real Estate Shuffle
themes.body: NASA's decision to select a new headquarters by year-end signals a potential shift in its operational focus. This move could reflect broader ambitions as the agency grapples with aging infrastructure and evolving mission needs.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy in Space
themes.body: With True Anomaly raising $190M and Apex hitting a $2.3B valuation, the space unicorns are multiplying. Investors seem keen to capitalize on the burgeoning demand for space services, despite the occasional hiccup in project timelines.

themes.title: Defense Tech IPOs on the Rise
themes.body: The defense-tech sector is showing signs of life as the IPO window cracks open, with companies like Palantir securing significant extensions. This could lead to a wave of public offerings, as investors seek to capitalize on the intersection of technology and national security.

themes.title: International Space Concerns
themes.body: NASA's worries about Russian repairs have prompted a safe haven decision for the ISS, highlighting geopolitical tensions in space. Meanwhile, co-orbital activities near commercial GEO slots raise eyebrows, suggesting that space is becoming as contentious as it is strategic.
